Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

phylogp (development version)

  • New kernel k_regime(): Brownian motion whose rate depends on discrete regimes (habitat, diet, selective regime) mapped on the tree, as in multi-rate Brownian motion (O’Meara et al. 2006). The regimes come from a phytools stochastic map given as the tree, including changes along a branch; phylo_gp_trees() integrates over a sample of maps. The kernel is branch-wise, so it keeps the linear-time likelihood, leave-one-out, prediction and ancestral states, and it can be fitted by maximum likelihood, where it reproduces phytools::brownie.lite(). Pruning a tree (species without data, prediction) keeps the map.
  • predict() now predicts species that were not fitted for every kernel, including those with latent values (k_relaxed(), k_rate_time(), latent k_slope() terms and k_white(df = )). The latent values a new species needs are drawn from their conditional prior given the fitted ones (a Brownian bridge along the fitted branch it joins, Brownian motion along its own branch, the prior for a Student-t multiplier).
  • Several rows per species can now be combined with known measurement error (se, one value per row): the species means are weighted by 1 / (within_sigma^2 + se^2), and the likelihood stays exact and linear.
  • Several rows per species can now be combined with a varying slope (k_slope(x) * k_bm(), latent): the slope acts on each row’s own x, and leave-one-out integrates the left-out species’ slope over all its rows in closed form.
  • data-raw/capabilities.R checks every kernel against every feature; the result is in the new “What works with what” article.
  • New vignette, “Several records per species, known errors and new species”, with worked examples of these three features.
  • “Designing kernels” has a new section, “New models from old parts”, with four sums of kernels: gradual plus speciational change, OU plus BM, an early burst that levels off, and phylogeny plus climate similarity, each with a check of whether its parts can be recovered.
  • Bug fix: loo() for fits across a sample of trees (phylo_gp_trees()) now runs PSIS-LOO on each tree and averages each species’ left-out density over trees, so trees are weighted equally, as documented. It used to run a single PSIS on the draws of all trees together, which weights each tree by the inverse of its predictive density for the left-out species (a harmonic mean across trees) and so underestimated elpd whenever trees differed in how well they predicted a species. The per-tree results are in attr(, "per_tree").
  • The paper is out as a preprint (EcoEvoRxiv, doi:10.32942/X2D99V); citation("phylogp") now gives it, with the software DOI.
  • References: the help pages of the kernel components and tools, the vignettes and the README now cite the work each model builds on (Brownian motion, the mixed model, Pagel’s transformations, early burst, OU, relaxed rates, spatial kernels, varying slopes, within-species variation, kernel validity, leave-one-out and prediction).
  • plot_effects() plots the expected response along each predictor, with a posterior credible band, over the data (like brms::conditional_effects(), named differently so both packages can be loaded together), and returns the values for custom plots.
  • New vignette, “A tour of models”: from Brownian motion and PGLS through the classical family, measurement error, several individuals per species, rates through time, phylogeny plus geography and outlying species, to model choice by leave-one-out and leave-clade-out cross-validation, prediction and ancestral states.
  • Several rows per species: with species = given, phylo_gp() accepts repeated measurements (e.g. individuals) and adds a within-species residual standard deviation, within_sigma. The kernel then describes the species and k_white() is the non-phylogenetic species effect, as in (1 | species) of a mixed model. The likelihood is exact and keeps its linear cost, because it factorises into the species means and the deviations from them; predictors may vary within species. Leave-one-out, loo_refit() and loo_group() leave out whole species, predict() includes the within-species variation in type = "response", and ancestral() works as before. Not yet available with varying slopes or known measurement error (se).
  • make_stancode(), make_standata() and stancode() are renamed kernel_stancode() and kernel_standata(), so that phylogp and brms can be loaded together without masking each other’s functions. kernel_stancode() takes a kernel or a fitted model (replacing stancode(fit)).

phylogp 0.2.0

  • kernel_equivalent() checks whether one kernel can reproduce the tip distribution of another: for each parameter setting of the first it searches over all parameters of the second for the smallest Kullback-Leibler divergence, comparing contrasts when the mean is unknown. It flags best-fitting parameters that sit at their bounds.

  • phylo_gp_trees() fits a model across a sample of trees and pools the posterior (or collects maximum-likelihood estimates), reporting how much of the uncertainty comes from the phylogeny; loo() works on the pooled fit.

  • loo_group() does leave-clade-out (or any leave-group-out) cross-validation: refits without each group and scores the group’s joint predictive density, in linear time for branch-wise kernels. Returns a kfold object for loo::loo_compare().

  • Tree matrices (incidence, shared path lengths, distances) are cached per tree_info() object.

  • predict() gives posterior predictions for fitted species and for species in the tree without data (kriging on the tree).

  • ancestral() reconstructs ancestral states in linear time; for OU it uses the OU process itself rather than its tip kernel.

  • loo_refit() replaces the PSIS-LOO contribution of influential species (high Pareto k) by an exact refit.

  • Varying slopes: k_slope(x) * k_bm() (or another branch-wise kernel) for slopes that evolve along the tree, fitted with latent node values in linear time or with the dense marginal kernel; k_slope(x) * k_white() as the heteroscedastic control. varying_slopes() summarises the slopes.

  • k_white(df = ): Student-t residuals for data with outlying species.

  • Leave-one-out integrates each species’ own latent values (slopes, rates, variance multipliers); k_relaxed() can now be combined with dense components.

  • plot_tree_values() colours a tree by any value.

  • New vignette: “Slopes, prediction and robust residuals”.

phylogp 0.1.0

  • First version.
  • Kernel grammar: classical kernels (k_bm(), k_lambda(), k_kappa(), k_delta(), k_eb(), k_ou(), k_white()), extensions (k_relaxed(), k_rate_time(), k_dist()) and user-defined branch-wise kernels (k_edge()), combined with +.
  • phylo_gp() writes, compiles and fits the Stan program by maximum likelihood or HMC, with an O(N) pruning likelihood and O(N) leave-one-out densities for branch-wise kernels.
  • Design tools: kernel_check(), kernel_plot(), kernel_matrix(), kernel_simulate(), kernel_loglik(), make_stancode().
  • Rate summaries: edge_rates(), plot_edge_rates(), plot_tree_rates(), rate_through_time().
  • Vignettes: “Getting started with phylogp” and “Designing kernels”.
